## Command Details

```text
Register read-only Adapters, record immutable read receipts, and prepare migration candidates (F051).
Adapters declare source owner, supported record types/versions, exact scope,
identity mapping, freshness, and read-only permissions. Pre-Cutover reads
never mutate Canonical Artifacts; migration candidates become normal Artifact admission payloads
and receipts record fresh/stale/unavailable/conflict/unmapped with exact source bytes/digest.
Shadow comparison writes bounded coverage receipts with source and target hashes.
Cutover is a separate human Decision scoped by artifact type, scope, and generation,
bound to resolved comparison evidence, a registered human owner's independent
confirmation, and rollback evidence naming a recorded Evidence receipt;
post-cutover source divergence appends a Finding and degrades reads and
migration candidates.

Subcommands:
  register --id <id> --adapter-owner <owner> --record-type <type>
        --record-version <v> --scope <scope> --identity-map <strategy>
        --freshness-ms <n> [--allow-path <prefix>] [--adapter-version <v>]
  read --id <id> --source <path> --record-id <id> [--record-type <type>] [--record-version <v>] [--expected-source-hash <hash>] [--scope <scope>]
  candidate --id <id> --source <path> --record-id <id> [--record-type <type>] [--record-version <v>] [--expected-source-hash <hash>] [--scope <scope>]
  compare --id <id> --fixture <json> [--scope <scope>]
  comparisons [--id <adapter-id>] [--scope <scope>]
  cutover --id <id> --cutover-id <id> --artifact-type <type> --generation <gen>
        --comparison-index <n> --decision-identity <identity> --revision <n>
        --confirmed-by <owner> --rollback-evidence <ref> [--scope <scope>]
  rollback --cutover-id <id> --decision-identity <identity> --revision <n>
        --confirmed-by <owner> --evidence <ref>
  cutovers [--id <adapter-id>] [--scope <scope>]
  show --id <id>
  list
  receipts [--id <adapter-id>]

Examples:
  amber adapter register --target . --id adapter/legacy --adapter-owner legacy-team --record-type legacy-ticket --record-version v1 --scope F051 --identity-map path --freshness-ms 86400000 --allow-path legacy --json
  amber adapter read --target . --id adapter/legacy --source legacy/item.json --record-id legacy-1 --record-version v1 --json
  amber adapter candidate --target . --id adapter/legacy --source legacy/item.json --record-id legacy-1 --record-version v1 --json
  amber adapter compare --target . --id adapter/legacy --fixture fixtures/adapter-shadow.json --json
  amber adapter cutover --target . --id adapter/legacy --cutover-id cutover/legacy-gen-1 --artifact-type intent --generation gen-1 --comparison-index 0 --decision-identity decision/cutover-legacy --revision 1 --confirmed-by legacy-team --rollback-evidence evidence/rollback-plan --json
```

## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines these target-relative paths, refusing `..` and symlink escapes before reading or writing: plan and scaffold destinations (including `accept --plan`), memory and context payloads, harness inputs, adapter allow-lists, workflow reports and their output directory, ledger exports, execution readiness plans, session and worktree state, governance report output, wiki export and handoff bundle output directories.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing, and the confinement above covers only the surfaces it names, and a confined flag still accepts an absolute destination only when it stays inside the target. `governance audit --output`, `governance readiness --output`, `security audit --output`, `loop record --output`, and `explain --markdown` resolve against the working directory instead of `--target`. A path flag not listed here is confined only when the command that reads it routes through the boundary. A governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions.
- `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess` and `governance report` reject output destinations that resolve to the target root, including `.`, an absolute root path, `nested/..`, and symlink or junction aliases of the root. Output subdirectories and defaults are unchanged.
- `wiki export` and `handoff bundle` check all planned file destinations and their parent directories before the first write, including copied wiki pages and optional replay files. An existing child symlink or junction outside the target refuses the export without changing output files. `wiki export` also checks every page it copies, so a page that shares its bytes with another name refuses the export before anything is written, including when both names stay inside the target. Concurrent link replacement is not prevented.
- A planned output file that shares its bytes with another name — a hard link, or a link to one — is refused before the write by `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess --output-dir`, `governance report --output`, `ledger export --out`, `knowledge context-review-sample --output`, `gate --plan` and `accept --plan` (the plan file they edit in place), `handoff` (the `session-handoff.md` it overwrites) and `hooks install` (the `pre-commit` hook it overwrites), even when both names stay inside the target. A link to a single in-target file is still written through, so it replaces that file's bytes; `workflow assess` is the exception, because it confines its output file to the `--output-dir` and so refuses a link whose referent sits elsewhere in the target. Like the child-link check above, this is checked before the write, so a link swapped in during the write is not caught.
- `handoff validate --bundle-dir .` and `workflow assess --handoff-bundle-dir .` still accept root-level bundles as read-only inputs. Explicit handoff validation paths outside `--target` are refused.
- Writing governance state goes through two shared helpers — the in-place JSON writer and the append-only JSONL ledger append — and both refuse a leaf that shares its bytes with another name. That covers the `.amber/` writers built on them (context pages and Loadouts, audit and event ledgers) without each one repeating the check; a raw write outside those helpers is guarded only where its own surface names it above.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
